messages:
From: Samantha Rhodes <samantha@catalogly.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick 15m stack compatibility check before demo

Hi Ethan,

We signed up for Redwood last week (self-serve) and love the sound of the Dedicated option. Before we lock in a full demo for our product team, our engineering lead asked for a very short technical check — 10–15 minutes — to confirm basic compatibility with our stack and any network prerequisites.

A few quick details to help you prep:
- Catalogly is running on GCP (us-central1) on Kubernetes 1.24 behind a private VPC.
- We plan to route inference through API gateway; want to confirm any IP allowlist / egress requirements.
- Workloads will be short (<512 tokens) but bursty; we care about cold-start latency.

Are you available for a 15-minute slot this week? Ideally we’d have a solutions engineer join so we can ask a couple of infra questions.

Thanks,
Samantha Rhodes
Product Ops / Catalogly

Hi Samantha — thanks for the note and for signing up! Glad Catalogly is trying Redwood. I can do a quick 15-minute compatibility check and I’ve looped Ben (solutions) so he can cover the infra specifics.

Here are a few slots that work on my side (PT):
- Tue Jul 1 — 10:00–10:15
- Tue Jul 1 — 14:00–14:15
- Wed Jul 2 — 09:30–09:45

If any of those work, I’ll send a calendar invite and attach a short pre-demo checklist that outlines the common network and auth items we usually confirm. Also: could you confirm whether the eng team prefers a call with audio only or wants screenshare for a quick network review?

Cheers,

Hi Ethan — thanks for the quick reply. 10:00–10:15 PT on Tue Jul 1 works great for us. I’ll invite our infra lead (eng@catalogly.com) — they’ll want screenshare so they can show our firewall rules if needed.

A couple of prep items for you so Ben has context:
- We prefer to keep data in us-central, no EU residency needs for this POC.
- We expect spikes to ~30 concurrent requests during peak test windows.
- We use OAuth2 mTLS for service-to-service calls; are there docs on token handling and retention?

If you can send the checklist and an invite, we’ll confirm on our side.

Regards,
Samantha
